That matters because Carignan can be blunt in the wrong hands; here it turns into black cherry, dried herbs, iron, and stony saltiness, with tannins that feel firm rather than coarse.

parsed.hook: Les Tosses is Carignan stripped to its granite-and-slate core: 100% Carignan from Priorat, where steep hills force low yields and push flavor into dark, savory intensity. The 2021, 2022, and 2019 all landed at 97 points, which tells you this is not a curiosity bottle — it is a serious benchmark for modern Priorat.
parsed.wine_summary:
Terroir al Limit built its reputation by treating Priorat less like a place for power and more like a place for precision. Les Tosses is the purest expression of that idea: Carignan Noir from a rugged Catalan landscape where old vines, thin soils, and drought stress naturally limit vigor and concentrate fruit. That matters because Carignan can be blunt in the wrong hands; here it turns into black cherry, dried herbs, iron, and stony saltiness, with tannins that feel firm rather than coarse.

This wine sits at the center of the current Priorat conversation: less extraction, more site, more lift. The 97-point run across multiple recent vintages makes the point clearly — Les Tosses is not chasing opulence for its own sake. It matters because it gives Carignan dignity and specificity, and because it offers a more exacting, less exaggerated version of Priorat than many wines built from the region’s more muscular template.
parsed.terroir_expression: Priorat’s signature llicorella — fractured slate and quartzite on steep slopes — drains fast and forces roots deep into narrow seams of moisture, which is why the wine tastes stony, compact, and tensile rather than lush. The Mediterranean climate brings heat and sun, but altitude and mountain breezes preserve acidity, so the fruit ripens fully without losing its edge. In the glass that means black fruit, iron, dried thyme, and a firm mineral line that reads like wet slate rather than sweet spice.
parsed.vinification_summary: The 2022 vintage sees 8 months in oak, a restrained élevage that supports structure without burying the fruit. That short oak contact matters in Carignan because the grape already carries a hard tannic frame; too much barrel can make it feel dry and monolithic. Managed carefully, oak rounds the edges, adds a little spice and mid-palate breadth, and leaves the wine’s herbal, mineral character in the foreground.
parsed.food_pairing:
Charred lamb chops with rosemary and garlic work because Carignan’s tannins grip protein and its dried-herb notes echo the rosemary.
Nashville hot chicken is a strong casual pairing: the wine’s acidity and dark fruit cool the chile burn while the tannin stands up to fried crust.
Duck confit with lentils and lentil salad suits the wine’s iron and earth tones, especially when the lentils bring their own savory depth.
Pigeon or squab with sour cherries and juniper fits a fine-dining setting because the wine’s dark fruit and herbal spine mirror the game bird and sharpen the fruit sauce.
Mushroom and pecorino risotto works well too: the wine’s slatey, savory finish meets the mushrooms halfway and keeps the dish from feeling heavy.
comparable_wines: Clos Mogador Manyetes — similar Priorat seriousness, but often broader and more Grenache-led in texture.
Mas Martinet Martinet Bru — another modern Priorat red with site-driven mineral tension and a polished but not plush profile.
Alvaro Palacios Les Terrasses — comparable in region and ambition, though typically a blend rather than the Carignan singularity of Les Tosses.
parsed.style_profile: 100% Carignan with medium-full body, firm tannins, and iron-slate savory depth
parsed.cellar_recommendation: Drink from now through the next 8 to 12 years if you want the wine’s tension and mineral drive; older bottles should gain more leather, olive, and dried herb complexity. Store cool and steady, because Priorat’s density can age well but heat damage flattens the wine’s lift quickly.
parsed.value_assessment: $120 to $180 puts Les Tosses in the serious single-vineyard Priorat bracket, where it competes with Clos Mogador, Clos Erasmus, and Alvaro Palacios’ top bottlings. It is worth the money if you want a Carignan-led wine with site clarity and ageworthy structure; if you want immediate plushness, your dollars go farther in a broader blend.
parsed.market_position: This is a bottle for collectors, sommeliers, and customers who already understand that Priorat can be about structure and mineral detail, not just volume. It belongs on high-end restaurant lists and in retail shops that sell terroir-driven Spanish wine by the bottle, because the wine’s point is specificity, not crowd-pleasing ease.
parsed.insider_take: The trap is treating Les Tosses like a power wine, because that misses what makes it special. It is firmer, leaner, and more architectural than the market expects from Priorat, and that is exactly why it works. People chasing sweetness of fruit should skip it; people who like Etna Rosso, structured Barolo, or serious northern Rhône reds will understand it fast.
